the use of SDS and acetone for membrane protein extraction resulted in the identification of 117 unique membrane proteins from Chloro­bium tepidum, of which 37 were predicted to have signal sequences indicating their localization in periplasm or outer membrane.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the extraction of membrane proteins, which can be used for proteome analysis of Chlorobium tepidalum and other photosynthetic organisms.
improving the analysis of the membrane proteins of Chlorobium tepidlum by the use of various extraction methods and the application of mass spectrometry.

the development and optimization of methods for the extraction, solubilization and separation of membrane proteins from C. tepidum and we have demonstrated that the combination of SDS solubilization with the acetone precipitation method is an efficient method for the analysis of the membrane proteome of this organism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of SDS for protein extraction and 2‐DE analysis is a valuable tool for membrane protein identification, but the method has to be used in conjunction with the acetone precipitation method.

the use of ionic SDS for solubilization of membrane proteins in conjunction with acetone precipitation of proteins prior to 2‐DE analysis is the method of choice to identify a maximum number of proteins.
a combination of the two methods is necessary in order to obtain a comprehensive view of the membrane proteome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of SDS and acetone precipitation in the solubilization of membrane proteins resulted in the detection of 154 proteins, of which 37 were identified to be localized in the outer membrane of C. tepidum.

the use of ionic detergent for protein extraction and the acetone precipitation of the supernatants improved the results by the detection of additional proteins, which were more difficult to solublize than the less hydrophobic ones.
a combination of the two methods of solubilization of membrane proteins, SDS and Triton X‐ 100, is the best approach for the enrichment of proteins from the membranes of C. tepidum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enrichment of membrane proteomes is not a simple procedure and that a combination of methods may be necessary to obtain the best results.

the enrichment of membrane‐associated proteins from C. tepidum is possible and can be achieved by the use of different methods, but the use of ionic detergent and the combination of SDS with acetone precipitation are the methods of choice.
the use of SDS in protein solubilisation combined with acetone in protein precipitation improves the 2‐DE membrane protein pattern and allows the identification of additional proteins.
